title: Arabic Wordplay and the Hidden Pun
text:
Classical Arabic poets prized the double meaning known as tawriya, in which a single word carries a near meaning that is obvious and a far meaning that is intended. A listener who catches only the obvious sense has missed the poet's wit, while one who grasps both is rewarded with a sudden flash of pleasure. The device was regarded less as an ornament than as proof that the speaker commanded the full resources of the language.

Modern readers encounter the same technique in translation, where the far meaning often disappears. A translator must therefore decide whether to preserve the ambiguity, find a comparable pun in the target language, or sacrifice the wordplay to keep the sense clear. Each choice involves loss, and critics debate which loss is most acceptable.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what does a tawriya contain?
options: A near meaning that is obvious and a far meaning that is intended
A quotation from an earlier poet

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what often disappears when the device is translated?
What does the passage imply about how the device was regarded in its original culture?
options: As a minor decoration with no value
As evidence of the speaker's command of the language
As a rule that only children followed
As a method of hiding the poet's identity

questions.text: Why might a translator face a difficult choice when rendering a tawriya?
options: Because every translation must be longer than the original
Because each option for keeping the ambiguity involves some loss
Because the target language has no words at all
Because critics forbid translation of poetry

vocabulary.definition: the quality of allowing more than one possible meaning
deliberately meant by the speaker or writer
a person who renders a text from one language into another
the clever and playful use of words and their meanings

paragraph_translations: كان الشعراء العرب الكلاسيكيون يقدّرون المزدوج المعنى المعروف بالتورية، إذ تحمل الكلمة الواحدة معنى قريبًا ظاهرًا وآخر بعيدًا مقصودًا. فالسامع الذي يلتقط المعنى الظاهر وحده يفوته ظرف الشاعر، أما من يدرك المعنيين فيكافأ بومضة مفاجئة من المتعة. وكان يُنظر إلى هذه الصنعة لا بوصفها زخرفة فحسب، بل دليلًا على أن المتكلم يملك موارد اللغة كاملة.

يلقى القراء المعاصرون التقنية نفسها في الترجمة، حيث يختفي المعنى البعيد في كثير من الأحيان. وعلى المترجم أن يقرر ما إذا كان سيحافظ على الغموض، أم يجد جناسًا مماثلًا في اللغة الهدف، أم يضحي بلعب الكلمات ليحفظ المعنى واضحًا. ينطوي كل خيار على خسارة، ويتجادل النقاد حول أيّ الخسائر أكثر قبولًا.
